differences.title: 1. PARSING EFFICIENCY
differences.leftDesc: Protocol Buffers requires deserialization into memory structures before data access, adding a processing step. This ensures type safety and ease of use.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers allows direct access to data in its serialized form without parsing. Fields are accessed via computed offsets, minimizing CPU overhead.

differences.title: 2. PAYLOAD SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Protobuf uses varints and field numbers for efficient encoding, resulting in very small payloads. Schema is embedded separately.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers includes schema information (offsets) directly within the buffer, leading to slightly larger payloads but enabling direct access.

differences.title: 3. SCHEMA EVOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Protobuf excels at schema evolution. Adding new fields or deprecating old ones maintains compatibility, allowing gradual updates to services.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers also supports schema evolution. New fields can be added, and old ones ignored, ensuring compatibility with older readers.

differences.title: 4. MEMORY USAGE
differences.leftDesc: Deserializing Protobuf messages into objects often involves memory allocations for the resulting data structures.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers requires minimal to no memory allocation for data access, as data is read directly from the buffer in place.

differences.title: 5. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Protobuf is widely used for inter-service communication (gRPC) and data persistence where deserialization overhead is acceptable.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers is ideal for performance-critical applications like game development and large dataset processing where low latency is paramount.

differences.title: 6. CODE GENERATION
differences.leftDesc: Protobuf compilers generate data classes and serialization/deserialization methods, simplifying object manipulation.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers compilers generate accessor methods for fields, allowing direct access without creating intermediate objects.

differences.title: 7. MUTABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Protobuf objects are typically mutable after deserialization, allowing for in-place modifications.
differences.rightDesc: FlatBuffers data is generally treated as immutable once read from the buffer, promoting safer concurrent access patterns.
